Regulatory Counsel, AI Regulation, US
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY

reading.body:
AI governance hiring here is five senior roles, four of them in US tech hubs, and only one names compute and infrastructure directly.

Every title carries a seniority marker: Senior Consultant, Principal, Staff, Lead, Counsel. There are no junior or mid-level openings in the set. The employers are a consultancy, two model developers, a data platform, and a workflow software vendor. Four roles sit in the United States, across San Francisco, Santa Clara, and New York, with one in Munich. The postings span April to September 2026.

The work is being hired inside the companies that build and sell compute-intensive systems, not inside regulators. That matters because governance obligations land on whoever operates the models and the infrastructure behind them, and those operators are staffing for it directly. The Cohere role is the only one that ties policy to compute, infrastructure, and sovereign AI in its title, which is the one visible thread between governance hiring and the physical buildout. A single posting is not evidence of a pattern.

Five postings cannot describe a market. The data carries no salary, no applicant volume, no breakdown of how many governance roles go unfilled, and no time series, so it cannot show whether this hiring is rising or falling. No government or regulatory-agency roles appear in the set, even though federal and aggregated sources are in scope, which may mean those jobs are classified elsewhere or simply were not captured. Read the seniority and the geography as the signal, and treat the count as a sample rather than a total.
